Eddie Pack ran the 440 yards stage and did well in handing over third behind Whittingham and Pallett. Stroud and Bone both did their bit in keeping this position; and Tommy went off about 30 yards behind the leaders, who were A.
Eddie Pack made a game effort but could never head his opponent; and Stroud's strength told in a close finish.

We all followed these events, now given in reverse order, with the greatest interest, and congratulate him upon these performances. We also congratulate Eddie Pack upon winning the Police 440 yards Championship at Bradford in fifty and seven-tenths seconds.

This was not too good from our point of view as regards point scoring, but we soon pulled up, gaining useful points when Fred White won the 880 yards, and Eddie Pack and Michael came home together in the 440 yards.
The 440 yards saw Eddie Pack run away from his field, and with A.
Congratulations to E.
Our team ran impressively in their heat, and in the final Eddie Pack gave our team a splendid start, unofficial watches timing him to do a shade outside 50 seconds.
In the County Championships, some of our men were seen to advantage. E.
Eddie Pack was also a starter in the 440 yards match, but was content to take things easy after his Middlesex County win the previous Saturday.

Pritchard, E.
Owing to our date clashing with the Police championships, we were denied the sight of Eddie Pack beating the club record of 51 secs. in the 440 yards championship.
In the 4 x 300 yds. we had Eddie Pack doing the last leg and although the shape of the track was not suitable to his huge stride, he soon put the issue beyond doubt.
Eddie Pack recorded 49 1-5 seconds in finishing fourth in the A.A.A. 440 yards Championship; and for the first time on record, a Club team was placed third in an A.A.A.
Eddie Pack did the quarter but did not extend himself, and the Ealing man gained slightly, but Les Bennett and Alec Mewes, our two sprinters, kept our lead to win a good race.
Eddie Pack ran for us in the 449 yards, and as befits the holder of the Middlesex County title, he won this event; with Syd Jarlett scoring a point for 4th place.
I hope our members will keep Eddie Pack busy by giving him a bumper entry. They include a 2 Miles Relay at this meeting, which is on handicap lines.

Congratulations also to Eddie Pack upon his selection to represent England at Dublin. Eddie has shown consistent form throughout the season, and he is unfortunate in having such a number of first-class quarter-milers contemporary with him.
While Eddie Pack was away in Scotland again winning the Police 440 yards Championship, Cadogan A.C. strove to retain the Middlesex Relay title.
In the 440 yards Eddie Pack refused to risk a breakdown owing to the loose surface; and for an athlete of his build his point of view can be readily understood.
In the final he was placed 4th, and so scored 3 points. Another fine performance was Eddie Pack’s running in the 440 yards, and after an easy heat win, he made A.
Further, Eddie Pack was in Belfast running for England in the triangular match there, and so lessened our chance of picking up points in the 440 yards event.

Our attention was then drawn to the High Jump, which was won by a member whose name is not usually associated with jumping—Eddie Pack. He cleared 5ft. 5in., and a junior, Len Marchant, was second with 5ft. 3in.; he will undoubtedly get higher, as his physique is well suited to this event.

We think of the superb Club track men such as Tommy Scrimshaw, Jim Tosh, George Dunckley, Eddie Pack, Cooper-Clark, Len Herbert; together with Bert Footer, Arthur Penny, Jim Ginty, Tom Carter, Les Cohen, Pat Parker, the Flowers, Jack and Joe, Arthur Allum.
Eddie Pack also made a welcome reappearance, and we hope he will soon regain the form which took him into an A.A.A. Final and a place in the Empire Games Team which visited Australia.
With the help of Teddy Fretwell and his Band and with Eddie Pack doing his stuff as M.C. over a hundred and sixty dancers took the floor at various times during the evening.
Eddie Pack was Southern and Inter-Counties 440 yards Champion, and runner-up in the A.A.A. title. Charlie Melchior was second in the Southern and third in the A.A.A.
We are sorry to hear that our pre-war quarter miler, Eddie Pack, has had an operation and has been " in dock " for several months. He is now back on duty again with the City Police.

Pat Parker was placed third in the 3 miles (14:28.0) and earned selection against France the following week. Don Brown was third and Percy Wright fourth in the 2 miles walk, and Eddie Pack (49.2) finished fourth in the final of the 440 yards.
Congratulations also to Eddie Pack upon his selection to represent England at Dublin. A few years ago Pack's times would have won A.A.A. titles.
